readings.title: The Two Offerings
readings.subtitle: The Murder of Abel and the Mark of Cain
readings.text: [Genesis 4:1] And Aḏam knew <dn>את</dn> Ḥavvah his wife, and she conceived and bore <dn>את</dn> Qayin, and said, “I have gained a man, <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [2] And again, she gave birth to <dn>את</dn> his brother <dn>את</dn> Heḇel. And Heḇel became a keeper of sheep, but Qayin became a tiller of the ground. [3] And it came to be, in the course of time, that Qayin brought an offering of the fruit of the ground to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] And Heḇel also brought of the first-born of his flock and of their fat. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looked to Heḇel and his offering, [5] but <dn>He</dn> did not look to Qayin and his offering. And Qayin was very wroth, and his face fell. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Qayin, <dq>“Why is he wroth towards you? And why is your face fallen?</dq> [7] <dq>“Is it not if you do good, you are to be accepted? And if you do not do good, towards the door is a sin. He is lying and towards you is his desire, and you must rule over him.”</dq> [8] And Qayin told Heḇel his brother. And it came to be when they were in the field, that Qayin rose up against Heḇel his brother and killed him. [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Qayin, <dq>“Where is Heḇel your brother?”</dq> And he said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s guard?” [10] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to <dn>Me</dn> from the ground.</dq> [11] <dq>“And now you are cursed from the earth, which has opened <dn>את</dn> its mouth to receive <dn>את</dn> your brother’s blood from your hand.</dq> [12] <dq>“If you till <dn>את</dn> the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”</dq> [13] And Qayin said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “My punishment is too great to bear! [14] “See, <dn>You</dn> have driven <dn>את</dn> me from the face of the ground today, and I am hidden from <dn>Your</dn> face. I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and it shall be that anyone who finds me kills me.” [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Well, if anyone kills Qayin, vengeance is taken on him sevenfold.”</dq> And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set up a sign for Qayin, lest anyone finding him strikes him. [16] So Qayin went out from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and dwelt in the land of Noḏ on the east of Ěḏen. [17] And Qayin knew <dn>את</dn> his wife, and she conceived and bore <dn>את</dn> Ḥanoḵ. And he built a city, and called <dn>את</dn> the name of the city after the name of his son, Ḥanoḵ. [18] And to Ḥanoḵ was born <dn>את</dn> Iraḏ. And Iraḏ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Meḥuya’ěl, and Meḥuya’ěl brought forth <dn>את</dn> Methusa’ěl, and Methusa’ěl brought forth <dn>את</dn> Lemeḵ. [19] And Lemeḵ took for himself two wives, the name of one was Aḏah, and the name of the second was Tsillah. [20] And Aḏah bore <dn>את</dn> Yaḇal. He was the father of those who dwell in tents, with livestock. [21] And his brother’s name was Yuḇal. He was the father of all those who play the lyre and flute. [22] As for Tsillah, she also bore <dn>את</dn> Tuḇal-Qayin, a smith of all kinds of tools in bronze and iron. And the sister of Tuḇal-Qayin was Na‛amah. [23] And Lemeḵ said to his wives, “Aḏah and Tsillah, hear my voice! Wives of Lemeḵ, listen to my words! For I have killed a man for wounding me, even a young man for hurting me. [24] “For Qayin is avenged sevenfold, and Lemeḵ seventy-sevenfold.” [25] And Aḏam knew <dn>את</dn> his wife again, and she bore a son and called <dn>את</dn> his name Shěth, “For <dn>Elohim</dn> has appointed me another seed instead of Heḇel, because Qayin had killed him.” [26] And to Shěth, to him also a son was born. And he called <dn>את</dn> his name Enosh. Then it was begun to call on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Generations of Adam
readings.subtitle: From Adam to Noah
readings.text: [Genesis 5:1] This is the book of the genealogy of Aḏam. In the day that <dn>Elohim</dn> created man, <dn>He</dn> made him in the likeness of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] Male and female <dn>He</dn> created them, and <dn>He</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> them, and called <dn>את</dn> their name ‘Aḏam’ in the day they were created. [3] And Aḏam lived one hundred and thirty years, and brought forth a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called <dn>את</dn> his name Shěth. [4] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shěth, the days of Aḏam were eight hundred years. And he brought forth sons and daughters. [5] So all the days that Aḏam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died. [6] And Shěth lived one hundred and five years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Enosh. [7] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Enosh, Shěth lived eight hundred and seven years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [8] So all the days of Shěth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died. [9] And Enosh lived ninety years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Qěynan. [10] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Qěynan, Enosh lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [11] So all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died. [12] And Qěynan lived seventy years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Mahalal’ěl. [13] After he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Mahalal’ěl, Qěynan lived eight hundred and forty years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [14] So all the days of Qěynan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died. [15] And Mahalal’ěl lived sixty-five years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yereḏ. [16] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yereḏ, Mahalal’ěl lived eight hundred and thirty years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [17] So all the days of Mahalal’ěl were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died. [18] And Yereḏ lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ḥanoḵ. [19] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ḥanoḵ, Yereḏ lived eight hundred years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [20] So all the days of Yereḏ were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died. [21] And Ḥanoḵ lived sixty-five years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Methushelaḥ. [22] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Methushelaḥ, Ḥanoḵ walked with <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> three hundred years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [23] So all the days of Ḥanoḵ were three hundred and sixty-five years. [24] And Ḥanoḵ walked with <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>. Then he was no more, for <dn>Elohim</dn> took <dn>את</dn> him. [25] And Methushelaḥ lived one hundred and eighty-seven years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Lemeḵ. [26] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Lemeḵ, Methushelaḥ lived seven hundred and eighty-two years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [27] So all the days of Methushelaḥ were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died. [28] And Lemeḵ lived one hundred and eighty-two years, and brought forth a son, [29] and called <dn>את</dn> his name Noaḥ, saying, “This one does comfort us concerning our work and the toil of our hands, because of the ground which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has cursed.” [30] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Noaḥ, Lemeḵ lived five hundred and ninety-five years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [31] So all the days of Lemeḵ were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died. [32] And Noaḥ was five hundred years old, and Noaḥ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shěm, <dn>את</dn> Ḥam, and <dn>את</dn> Yapheth.

readings.title: The Lineage of the Nations
readings.subtitle: From Adam to Edom
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 1:1] Aḏam, Shěth, Enosh, [2] Qěnan, Mahalal’ěl, Yereḏ, [3] Ḥanoḵ, Methushelaḥ, Lemeḵ, [4] Noaḥ, Shěm, Ḥam, and Yapheth. [5] The sons of Yapheth: Gomer, and Maḡoḡ, and Maḏai, and Yavan, and Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ, and Tiras. [6] And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Diphath, and Toḡarmah. [7] And the sons of Yavan: Elishah and Tarshishah, Kittim and Roḏanim. [8] The sons of Ḥam: Kush and Mitsrayim, Put and Kena‛an. [9] And the sons of Kush: Seḇa, and Ḥavilah, and Saḇta, and Ra‛mah, and Saḇteḵa. And the sons of Ra‛mah: Sheḇa and Deḏan. [10] And Kush brought forth <dn>את</dn> Nimroḏ; he began to be a mighty one on the earth. [11] And Mitsrayim brought forth <dn>את</dn> the Luḏim, and <dn>את</dn> the Anamim, and <dn>את</dn> the Lehaḇim, and <dn>את</dn> the Naphtuḥim, [12] and <dn>את</dn> the Pathrusim, and <dn>את</dn> the Kasluḥim from whom came the Philistines, and <dn>את</dn> the Kaphtorim. [13] And Kena‛an brought forth <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏon, his first-born, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥěth, [14] and <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusite, and <dn>את</dn> the Amorite, and <dn>את</dn> the Girgashite, [15] and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥivvite, and <dn>את</dn> the Arqite, and <dn>את</dn> the Sinite, [16] and <dn>את</dn> the Arvaḏite, and <dn>את</dn> the Tsemarite, and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥamathite. [17] The sons of Shěm: Ěylam, and Asshur, and Arpaḵshaḏ, and Luḏ, and Aram, and Uts, Ḥul, and Gether, and Mesheḵ. [18] And Arpaḵshaḏ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shelaḥ, and Shelaḥ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ěḇer. [19] To Ěḇer were born two sons: the name of one was Peleḡ, for in his days the earth was divided, and his brother’s name was Yoqtan. [20] And Yoqtan brought forth <dn>את</dn> Almoḏaḏ, and <dn>את</dn> Sheleph, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥatsarmaveth, and <dn>את</dn> Yeraḥ, [21] and <dn>את</dn> Haḏoram, and <dn>את</dn> Uzal, and <dn>את</dn> Diqlah, [22] and <dn>את</dn> Ěyḇal, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇima’ěl, and <dn>את</dn> Sheḇa, [23] and <dn>את</dn> Ophir, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥavilah, and <dn>את</dn> Yoḇaḇ. All these were the sons of Yoqtan. [24] Shěm, Arpaḵshaḏ, Shělah, [25] Ěḇer, Peleḡ, Re‛u, [26] Seruḡ, Naḥor, Teraḥ, [27] and Aḇram, that is Aḇraham. [28] The sons of Aḇraham: Yitsḥaq and Yishma‛ěl. [29] These are their genealogies: The first-born of Yishma‛ěl was Neḇayoth, and Qěḏar, and Aḏbe’ěl, and Miḇsam, [30] Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, Haḏaḏ, and Těma, [31] Yetur, Naphish, and Qěḏemah. These were the sons of Yishma‛ěl. [32] And the sons born to Qeturah, Aḇraham’s concubine: Zimran, and Yoqshan, and Meḏan, and Miḏyan, and Yishbaq, and Shuvaḥ. The sons of Yoqshan: Sheḇa and Deḏan. [33] And the sons of Miḏyan: Ěphah, and Ěpher, and Ḥanoḵ, and Aḇiḏa, and Elda‛ah. All these were the children of Qeturah. [34] And Aḇraham brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq. The sons of Yitsḥaq: Ěsav and Yisra’ěl. [35] The sons of Ěsav: Eliphaz, Re‛u’ěl, and Ye‛ush, and Ya‛lam, and Qoraḥ. [36] And the sons of Eliphaz: Těman, and Omar, Tsephi, and Gatam, and Qenaz, and Timna, and Amalěq. [37] The sons of Re‛u’ěl: Naḥath, Zeraḥ, Shammah, and Mizzah. [38] And the sons of Sě‛ir: Lotan, and Shoḇal, and Tsiḇ‛on, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ětser, and Dishan. [39] And the sons of Lotan: Ḥori and Homam; Lotan’s sister was Timna. [40] The sons of Shoḇal: Alyan, and Manaḥath, and Ěyḇal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Tsiḇ‛on: Ayah and Anah. [41] The son of Anah was Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Ḥamran, and Eshban, and Yithran, and Keran. [42] The sons of Ětser: Bilhan, and Za‛avan, and Ya‛aqan. The sons of Dishan: Uts and Aran. [43] And these were the sovereigns who reigned in the land of Eḏom before any sovereign reigned over the children of Yisra’ěl: Bela son of Be‛or, and the name of his city was Dinhaḇah. [44] And when Bela died, Yoḇaḇ son of Zeraḥ of Botsrah reigned in his place. [45] And Yoḇaḇ died, and Ḥusham of the land of the Těmanites reigned in his place. [46] And when Ḥusham died, Haḏaḏ son of Beḏaḏ, who struck <dn>את</dn> Miḏyan in the field of Mo’aḇ, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith. [47] And Haḏaḏ died, and Samlah of Masrěqah reigned in his place. [48] And Samlah died, and Sha’ul of Reḥoḇoth-by-the-River reigned in his place. [49] And Sha’ul died, and Ba‛al-Ḥanan son of Aḵbor reigned in his place. [50] And Ba‛al-Ḥanan died, and Haḏaḏ reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Pai. And his wife’s name was Mehětaḇ’ěl the daughter of Matrěḏ, the daughter of Měyzahaḇ. [51] And Haḏaḏ died. And the chiefs of Eḏom were Chief Timnah, Chief Alyah, Chief Yethěth, [52] Chief Oholiḇamah, Chief Ělah, Chief Pinon, [53] Chief Qenaz, Chief Těman, Chief Miḇtsar, [54] Chief Maḡdi’ěl, and Chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Eḏom.

readings.title: The Nephilim and the Ark
readings.subtitle: The Command to Build
readings.text: [Genesis 6:1] And it came to be, when men began to increase on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them, [2] that the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> the daughters of men, that they were good. And they took wives for themselves of all whom they chose. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>My</dn> Spirit shall not strive with man forever in his going astray. He is flesh, and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”</dq> [4] The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> came in to the daughters of men and they bore children to them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, the men of name. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was sorry that <dn>He</dn> had made <dn>את</dn> man on the earth, and <dn>He</dn> was grieved in <dn>His</dn> heart. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am going to wipe off <dn>את</dn> man whom <dn>I</dn> have created from the face of the ground, both man and beast, creeping creature and birds of the heavens, for <dn>I</dn> am sorry that <dn>I</dn> have made them.”</dq> [8] But Noaḥ found favour in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [9] This is the genealogy of Noaḥ. Noaḥ was a righteous man, perfect in his generations. Noaḥ walked with <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>. [10] And Noaḥ brought forth three sons: <dn>את</dn> Shěm, <dn>את</dn> Ḥam, and <dn>את</dn> Yapheth. [11] And the earth was corrupt before <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the earth was filled with violence. [12] And <dn>Elohim</dn> looked upon <dn>את</dn> the earth and saw that it was corrupt – for all flesh had corrupted <dn>את</dn> their way on the earth – [13] and <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Noaḥ, <dq>“The end of all flesh has come before <dn>Me</dn>, for the earth is filled with violence through them. And see, <dn>I</dn> am going to destroy them from the earth.</dq> [14] <dq>“Make yourself an ark of gopherwood. Make rooms in <dn>את</dn> the ark, and cover <dn>את</dn> it inside and outside with a covering.</dq> [15] <dq>“And this is how you are to make <dn>את</dn> it: The length of the ark is three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.</dq> [16] <dq>“Make a window for the ark, and complete it to a cubit from above. And set the door of the ark in its side. Make it with lower, second, and third decks.</dq> [17] <dq>“And see, <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> floodwaters on the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens – all that is on the earth is to die.</dq> [18] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> you, and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with <dn>את</dn> you.</dq> [19] <dq>“And of all the living of all flesh, two of each, you are to bring into the ark, to keep them alive with <dn>את</dn> you – a male and a female.</dq> [20] <dq>“Of the birds after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, and of all creeping creatures of the ground after their kind, two of each are to come to you, to keep them alive.</dq> [21] <dq>“As for you, take of all food that is eaten and gather it to yourself. And it shall be food for you and for them.”</dq> [22] And Noaḥ did according to all that <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> him, so he did.
